repo_notes.author: DevinWorkshop maintainers
repo_notes.content: PiggyMetrics is a legacy reference implementation of microservices on Spring Boot 2.0.3 / Spring Cloud Finchley with Netflix OSS (Eureka, Zuul 1, Ribbon, Hystrix, Turbine), Feign, Sleuth and spring-security-oauth2. Readers are engineers learning the architecture or planning its modernization: explain how the pieces interact at runtime and cite the code, instead of paraphrasing README.md. Treat config/src/main/resources/shared/*.yml (served by the Config Server with the native profile) as the source of truth for ports, routes, timeouts, cron expressions, OAuth2 clients and service URLs, and cite those files. Ports: gateway 4000 (published as 80), registry 8761, config 8888, auth-service 5000 (/uaa), account-service 6000 (/accounts), statistics-service 7000 (/statistics), notification-service 8000 (/notifications), turbine-stream-service 8080 (no server.port is set; docker-compose.yml publishes 8989:8989), monitoring 8080 (published as 9000), RabbitMQ 5672/15672, one MongoDB per service on 27017. OAuth2 clients (auth-service OAuth2AuthorizationConfig): browser (password + refresh_token, scope ui) and account-service / statistics-service / notification-service (client_credentials + refresh_token, scope server). Feign clients: account-service -> auth-service (AuthServiceClient) and statistics-service (StatisticsServiceClient with StatisticsServiceClientFallback); notification-service -> account-service (AccountServiceClient); statistics-service -> api.exchangeratesapi.io (ExchangeRatesClient with ExchangeRatesClientFallback).

repo_notes.author: DevinWorkshop maintainers
repo_notes.content: Flag anything legacy, end-of-life or broken today instead of presenting it as current, and link to the Known Issues & Workarounds page. Specifically: the build requires JDK 8; every Dockerfile uses the java:8-jre base image, which was removed from Docker Hub (eclipse-temurin:8-jre is a drop-in replacement, e.g. by retagging it as java:8-jre); .travis.yml (dist: trusty, oraclejdk8, encrypted Docker Hub credentials) and the sqshq/* images pulled by docker-compose.yml come from the upstream project and are not run or published by this repository; api.exchangeratesapi.io now requires an access key, so the landing page (gateway static/js/launch.js) shows NaN and statistics-service cannot fetch rates in ExchangeRatesServiceImpl; the ELK log analysis stack and Zipkin server mentioned in README.md are not part of this repository (only spring-cloud-starter-sleuth is on the classpath); the passwords in .env are development defaults. Spring Boot 2.0.x, Spring Cloud Finchley, Zuul 1, Ribbon, Hystrix and spring-security-oauth2 are end-of-life or in maintenance mode.

repo_notes.author: DevinWorkshop maintainers
repo_notes.content: Writing conventions: parent pages are short navigation summaries (what the section covers, how its child pages relate, one diagram) and must not repeat child page content. Every service page uses the same structure: responsibility, REST endpoints (method, path, required OAuth2 scope from @PreAuthorize), domain model and MongoDB collections, configuration keys from its shared/*.yml, outbound calls (Feign client, fallback, Hystrix/Ribbon settings) and tests under src/test. Prefer sequence diagrams for request flows and tables for ports, routes, endpoints, config keys and known issues. Do not spend pages or detail on static assets (fonts, sprites, images, CSS), .gitignore, LICENCE or issue templates; mention them in one line at most.

pages.title: Overview
pages.purpose: What PiggyMetrics is, the functional vs infrastructure service split, a service topology diagram, the Maven module map (one row per module with its port and role), and a reading guide to the rest of the wiki

pages.title: Architecture & Service Topology
pages.purpose: How the services are wired at runtime: Config Server bootstrap (bootstrap.yml in every module), Eureka registration and lookup, Zuul routing, OAuth2 token issuance and validation, RabbitMQ as the Turbine transport, and startup ordering and healthchecks in docker-compose.yml

pages.title: End-to-End Request Flows
pages.purpose: Sequence diagrams of the main user and system flows across gateway, auth-service, account-service, statistics-service and notification-service

page_notes.content: Cover at least: (1) login: the browser gets a password-grant token from /uaa/oauth/token through the gateway (login.js); (2) registration: POST /accounts/ creates the user in auth-service through AuthServiceClient, then saves the account; (3) saving the account: PUT /accounts/current, then StatisticsServiceClient.updateStatistics, falling back to StatisticsServiceClientFallback when statistics-service is down; (4) the notification-service scheduled jobs (remind.cron and backup.cron in shared/notification-service.yml) that call account-service with a client_credentials token and send email. Cite the controllers, Feign clients and services involved.

pages.title: Getting Started & Local Development
pages.purpose: Build and run locally: prerequisites, mvn package, docker-compose.yml with docker-compose.dev.yml, the .env password variables, published ports and the important URLs

page_notes.content: State the prerequisites explicitly: JDK 8 (newer JDKs fail with Boot 2.0.3), Maven and Docker with Compose. Explain the difference between production mode (docker-compose.yml alone pulls sqshq/* images) and development mode (adding docker-compose.dev.yml builds local images and publishes service, RabbitMQ and Mongo ports 25000-28000). Include one table with every published port from both compose files. Point out that java:8-jre must be replaced or retagged before docker compose --build works, and link to Known Issues & Workarounds.

pages.title: Known Issues & Workarounds
pages.purpose: What is broken or outdated when running the repository today: symptom, root cause in code or config, and workaround

page_notes.content: Use a table with Symptom / Cause / Workaround columns and one row per issue: removed java:8-jre base image; exchangeratesapi.io requiring an access key (NaN on the landing page from launch.js, no rates in ExchangeRatesServiceImpl, ExchangeRatesClientFallback behaviour); the Hystrix dashboard stream URL must be http://turbine-stream-service:8080/turbine/turbine.stream because the dashboard fetches the stream server-side, so localhost:8989 does not work; Travis CI pipeline and sqshq/* images not maintained here; JDK 8 requirement; development-only passwords in .env.

pages.purpose: The Account, Item, Saving, Currency and TimePeriod model duplicated in account-service and statistics-service, and how StatisticsServiceImpl normalizes amounts to a base currency and time period into DataPoint, ItemMetric and StatisticMetric time series

pages.purpose: monitoring module (Hystrix dashboard) and turbine-stream-service (WebFlux/Netty Turbine stream fed over RabbitMQ): how metrics flow from the services, and the stream URL to use in the dashboard

page_notes.content: Focus on the JavaScript behaviour and its API calls. Mention CSS, fonts and images in a single sentence; do not list asset files.
